problem: Robot memory representations such as metric maps, scene graphs and retrieval-augmented episodic memories (ReMEmbR, Enter the Mind Palace) are object-centric or short-horizon. They do not track persistent human identities across days or model recurring routines. As a result, a robot cannot answer questions like 'when does X usually arrive' or predict where a person is likely to be when searching for them.
motivation: Offices and homes are structured by recurring human behavior: people arrive and leave at regular times, use preferred locations and interact with objects habitually. Long-term deployed robots must reason over multi-day observations of this behavior. Feeding the full observation log to an LLM is token-expensive and dilutes attention, particularly for spatial grounding. This motivates structured, identity-aware memory with targeted retrieval, built concurrently with querying so the memory stays up to date.
key_idea: Continuously build an identity-aware, multi-day memory of captioned, waypoint- and time-stamped robot observations, with people clustered by face (DBSCAN) plus body ReID. Then let an LLM agent answer human-routine questions and pick navigation waypoints by iteratively calling a small set of structured retrieval functions instead of reading the full log.
insight: Targeted multi-granularity retrieval mitigates context dilution. The full-context Gemini 3 Flash baseline (631,651 tokens/question) reaches only 34.62% on spatial questions, versus 92.31% for HUMEMBR with the same LLM at 106,347 tokens, because every log entry contains similar waypoint tokens. The ablations show that identity-aware memory and the higher-level functions matter most for person and semantic questions. Removing ReID drops Total accuracy 66.01→60.49 (Person 57.14→48.57, Spatial 78.21→60.25). Restricting to 3 core functions drops Person 57.14→44.76 and Semantic 59.34→51.85, though Spatial and Duration slightly rise. A function-call limit of 10 is best for both Qwen3-VL-235B and Gemini (more calls add noise), and interaction-centered caption prompts beat hand-focused and movement-aware ones (66.01 vs 63.52 / 64.69).
method: Frame filtering: the 2 Hz RGB stream (stitched Spot front cameras) is passed through a ResNet50 encoder, and a frame is discarded if its cosine similarity to the last retained frame exceeds a threshold; each retained entry stores the image, GraphNav waypoint reference and timestamp.

Semantic captioning & indexing: each retained image is captioned by Qwen3-VL-235B (interaction-centered prompt performed best), and captions are embedded with mxbai-embed-large-v1 for similarity search.

Identity-aware person memory: YOLO person detection (gated on enough visible keypoints), InsightFace face embeddings and KPR (Keypoint Promptable ReID) full-body embeddings; in a two-stage unsupervised association, online DBSCAN clusters face embeddings into identity anchors, then face-less detections are attached to clusters via nearest-neighbor ReID matching under a similarity threshold.

Structured retrieval functions for the LLM agent: semantic observations (top-30 scored by s_i = α·cosine distance + β·(1−exp(−λΔt/3600)) recency term à la Generative Agents, optional person/time filter); waypoint observations in [t_s,t_e]; person observations in [t_s,t_e]; persons-per-day; LLM-generated daily summary per person.

Iterative tool-calling agent: the LLM (Gemini 3 Flash or Qwen3 variants) repeatedly calls the retrieval functions until it has enough evidence or hits a function-call limit (default 10), then answers.

Embodied control interface: a navigate_to_waypoint(W, P) function sends the robot to a GraphNav waypoint and optionally verifies person P on arrival; low-level motion is handled by the Boston Dynamics GraphNav stack, closing the loop between reasoning, retrieval and action.

Concurrency and benchmark: memory building and querying run in parallel in real time. The authors also contribute the COBD dataset (20 days, 31 h, >13,000 images, 136 waypoints) and PersonEQA (200 questions across six answer types).

numbers_note: PersonEQA is the authors' own 200-question benchmark with no official splits; 'test' denotes the frozen test set. Metrics are per-category accuracies with tolerances: spatial within 5 m, time/duration ±5 min, descriptive graded by an LLM (Semantic column), person sets must match exactly. HUMEMBR results are 3-seed means (± std omitted here). The full-context baseline (Gemini 3 Flash, all captions: Total 67.33, Spatial 34.62, 631,651 tokens) uses a single seed. Ablations not listed above: –ReID Total 60.49; 3 functions Total 63.04; function-call limits 5/10/15 (Qwen 62.29/66.01/65.07, Gemini 73.88/75.41/74.59); caption prompts (hand-focused 63.52, interaction-centered 66.01, movement-aware 64.69). Minor inconsistency: Gemini Time is 65.94 in Table I but 65.95 in Table II. The real-world table also reports duration, waypoints visited, function calls, first-visit detection, direct path % and tokens. The second deployment environment is mentioned but not reported separately.
results: On PersonEQA, HUMEMBR with Gemini 3 Flash reaches 75.41% total accuracy using 106,347 tokens/question. The full-context Gemini 3 Flash baseline reaches 67.33% at 631,651 tokens, so HUMEMBR uses about 83% fewer tokens, and spatial accuracy jumps from 34.62% to 92.31%. The baseline remains better on person identification (65.71 vs 60.95) and time questions (67.39 vs 65.94). The open-source Qwen3-VL-235B configuration nearly matches the baseline (66.01%) with about 2% of its tokens. On a real Spot robot, success rates range from 50% (partially occluded people) to 100% (visitor pick-up, package delivery) across six tasks × 10 runs.
limitations: Perception is the main failure mode: face detection and ReID break under occlusion, back views and poor lighting (50% SR on the occlusion task), and the agent can hallucinate prior sightings when the target person is absent.

The evaluation is narrow and in-house: a single office site, 200 questions, and one full-context baseline run on a single seed. The agent reasons only over text captions (no direct visual input or room labels), and the authors admit results are currently 'comparable to the baseline'.
The method relies on a pre-built GraphNav map and extensive prior multi-day recordings of the same site and its people, and persistent routine tracking raises privacy concerns.
compares_to: Full-context LLM baseline (all captions in context, Gemini 3 Flash)
